ARTH 101.course_name: Ways of Seeing: Introduction to Visual Studies
ARTH 101.description: Drawing on examples from across history and around the world, this course deals with the role of the visual in society, culture, and everyday experience.

ARTH 102.description: Introduction to the histories of art and the built environment in a global context.

ARTH 210.description: Art, architecture, and material culture of the Byzantine Empire situated in the eastern Mediterranean (c. 300-1453); focus on social and cultural contexts of artistic production, including interactions with neighboring cultures. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 210, CNRS 207 or AMNE 279. Equivalency: AMNE 279

ARTH 225.course_name: Art, Patrons, and Audiences in the Middle Ages
ARTH 225.description: A thematic study of the relationship between patrons and audiences in painting, sculpture, and architecture through the 15th century.

ARTH 226.description: Tensions and conflicts resulting from the expansion of trade and encounters among cultures, ethnicities, and religious practices, explored in visual art and architecture from the sixteenth century to the advent of the modern era.

ARTH 227.description: Select issues in 20th-century art and the visual and built environment.

ARTH 230.description: Feminist art and visual culture, from the political activism of the feminist first wave to its intersections with present-day social justice movements.

ARTH 251.course_name: Asian Arts: From Chinese Warriors to Bollywood Posters
ARTH 251.description: A thematic examination of Asian arts, such as historic, religious, and secular painting and sculpture to contemporary visual culture.

ARTH 253.course_name: Asian Architecture: Sacred and Urban Spaces
ARTH 253.description: Select built forms in Asia, such as temples, tombs, palaces, cities and gardens, and their relations to cultural, social and political systems.

ARTH 261.course_name: Pre-Hispanic Arts of Central and South America
ARTH 261.description: The relevance of various arts to social institutions in ancient societies of Peru and Mesoamerica.

ARTH 262.description: A survey of the artistic production by Indigenous peoples of North America from pre-contact times to the present.

ARTH 285.description: Intersections between visual art and the moving image in both a theoretical and historical context.

ARTH 297.description: Thematic and issue-based courses in art history. Topics vary year to year.

ARTH 300.course_name: Seminar on Methods and Approaches in Art History
ARTH 300.description: Theories, problems, and literature in the study of art history. Required of all Major and Honours students in art history. Prerequisite: 3 credits of ARTH_V coursework at any level. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

ARTH 309.course_name: Arts of Africa and the African Diasporas
ARTH 309.description: Comparative exploration of art practices and their relationship to colonial and postcolonial histories. Credit will be granted for only one of ARTH_V 309 or AFST_V 309. Equivalency: AFST_V 309.

ARTH 310.course_name: Art and the Religious Transformation of the Late Roman Empire
ARTH 310.description: Visual culture and religious diversity of the Late Roman Empire (2nd-7th c.); social, political, and religious contexts of art, including diverse viewing practices and cultural frameworks. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 310, CNRS 333 or AMNE 379. Equivalency: AMNE 379

ARTH 311.description: From pagan adornment to Christian devotion to service of Christian or Islamic rule (AD 500-1000). Art and architecture of the Early Medieval world's diverse and transforming social, political, cultural contexts.

ARTH 312.course_name: Medieval Art in the Age of Monasticism
ARTH 312.description: Art in Europe between 1000 and 1200; the role of monasteries as leading institutions and patrons of art and large-scale architecture.

ARTH 313.course_name: Art, Church, Society and their Margins in the Later Middle Ages
ARTH 313.description: Diversification of the arts and architecture with the expansion of patronage in late medieval society. Credit will be granted for only one of ARTH_V 313 or ARTH_V 333.

ARTH 319.course_name: The Archaeology of Ancient Iraq and Syria: Babylon and Beyond
ARTH 319.description: An overview of the archaeology of the ancient Near East, with special emphasis on the civilizations of Mesopotamia, from the appearance of the first cities (c. 3400 BCE) to the end of the Persian period (c. 330 BCE). AMNE 170 recommended as preparation. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 319, NEST 319, or AMNE 372 Equivalency: AMNE 372

ARTH 320.course_name: Entangled Worlds: Spain and Colonial Latin America (1500-1700)
ARTH 320.description: Role of visual art and culture within Catholic Spain and colonial Latin America is surveyed, with emphasis on transculturation from mudejar to mestizaje.

ARTH 321.course_name: Public and Private Bodies: Italian Renaissance Art and Culture
ARTH 321.description: Visual art and culture within the social, political, and religious contexts of the Papacy and the city-states ca. 1350-1550 (Siena, Florence, Venice, Mantua).

ARTH 322.course_name: Early Modern Italian Art and Culture (ca. 1550-1700)
ARTH 322.description: Focus primarily on Rome as the center of artistic, cultural, economic, and religious power in the seventeenth century.

ARTH 323.course_name: Heaven and Earth: Renaissance Art and Culture in Northern Europe
ARTH 323.description: Early Modern painting, sculpture, and the graphic arts from the great devotional triptychs, through the Reformation, to the emergence of a secular art (1400-1600).

ARTH 324.course_name: Urban and Courtly Arts in Early Modern Northern Europe (1600-1700)
ARTH 324.description: The role of visual art in 17th century court cultures, commercial urban centres, and emergent nation states.

ARTH 325.course_name: Ancient Egypt: The Archaeology of the Land of the Pharaohs
ARTH 325.description: The material remains of the ancient Egyptians from monumental tombs and temples to the artifacts of daily life; the development of Egyptian civilization from the rise of the first rulers to its incorporation into the Roman Empire. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 325, NEST 304, or AMNE 371. Equivalency: AMNE 371

ARTH 331.description: Visual culture of the ancient Greek world in the second and first millennia BCE, especially from c. 1000 to 30 BCE. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 331, CLST 331, or AMNE 376. Equivalency: AMNE 376

ARTH 332.description: Visual culture of the ancient Roman world from the 8th century BCE to the 4th century CE. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 332, CLST 332, or AMNE 377. Equivalency: AMNE 377

ARTH 338.course_name: Visual Culture in the Age of Enlightenment and Revolution (1715-1830)
ARTH 338.description: Art, architecture, and social space in Europe and America: redefining gender, identity and nation in the era of industrialization and political change.

ARTH 339.description: Ideologies of gender, class, race, ethnicity, and economics in 19th-century European and American visual culture.

ARTH 340.course_name: 20th Century Art and Culture: The Triumph and Demise of Modernism
ARTH 340.description: A critical survey of western art and cultural production from the turn of the century to the development of Pop Art.

ARTH 341.course_name: 20th Century Art and Culture: The Postmodern
ARTH 341.description: A critical examination of international visual art and culture from the 1950s to the present; the role of art in consumerist society and the emergence of postmodernism.

ARTH 342.course_name: Latin American Art: Modern and Contemporary
ARTH 342.description: Analyses of specific works and texts will emphasize visual inventions and meaning in the light of recent theoretical debates

ARTH 343.description: The institutions and art movements that constructed a view to the country now known as Canada, from colonial contact, to Confederation, through the mid-1900s. Emphasis on the significance of locality and situated approaches to understanding the land.

ARTH 344.course_name: Contemporary Conversations about Art in Kanata/Canada
ARTH 344.description: Radical shifts in thinking about Canadian art and culture since the mid-20th century. The art movements, debates, and institutions that contribute to the complexity of artistic approaches to representing Canada today.

ARTH 345.course_name: History of Photography: Archive, Spectacle, Reality
ARTH 345.description: History and theory of photography, from the competitive context of invention in the 1830s to contemporary uses in social media.

ARTH 346.course_name: Architecture in Europe: Building the Fabric of the Modern State (1715-1837)
ARTH 346.description: The role of architecture within the development of the modern state. A survey of broad cultural dynamics, particular building projects and design careers.

ARTH 347.course_name: Architecture in Europe: Modern Paradigms of Design (1837-present)
ARTH 347.description: An examination of new requirements imposed on architecture by the consolidation of a capitalist economy, industrialization, new technologies and scientific methods.

ARTH 348.course_name: Architecture in North America: Colonial Projects and Disruptions (1605-1867)
ARTH 348.description: The role of architecture in the imposition of European governance within North America; the modification of received conventions in relation to topographical, ethnic-religious and political factors.

ARTH 349.course_name: Architecture in North America: Independent Design Idioms (1867-present)
ARTH 349.description: The emergence of a distinctive architecture that superseded British and European agendas; the growth of private and public patronage and the establishment of modern design and practice.

ARTH 350.description: Contextualizing the complex language of images in the Islamic world.

ARTH 351.course_name: Art and Urban Culture in the Islamic World
ARTH 351.description: A thematic and comparative study of visual arts and architecture in their urban contexts.

ARTH 352.course_name: Historic India: Images, Temples and the Construction of Indian Art History
ARTH 352.description: North and South Indian art and architecture with an emphasis on Buddhism and Hinduism.

ARTH 353.course_name: Nepal and Tibet: Art, Ritual and Performance
ARTH 353.description: Art of the Himalayan region situated within social and religious practices, festivals, and performances.

ARTH 354.course_name: Mughal India: Art, Architecture and the Spectacle of Empire
ARTH 354.description: The complex relationship of Mughal imperial architecture and painting with those of the Hindu Rajput courts.

ARTH 355.course_name: Modern and Contemporary India: Art in Colonial and Independent India
ARTH 355.description: The development of a new Indian art during the colonial period and nationalist movement; the construction of India's contemporary visual culture.

ARTH 357.course_name: Chinese Art and Architecture: Patronage and Collecting
ARTH 357.description: The commission, production, preservation, and transmission of Chinese monuments and artworks focusing on the court and questions of cultural policies.

ARTH 358.description: Close analyses of Chinese tomb objects and tombs as spatial constructs in their historical, ritual, and social context.

ARTH 360.description: Analyses visual narratives and relationships between painting, calligraphy, and poetry in court and literati painting.

ARTH 361.description: Chinese art and its global entanglements from Qing Encounters to the 21st century.

ARTH 362.course_name: Art in Japan: Objects and Spaces
ARTH 362.description: Changing relationship between art objects and the built environment in the Japanese archipelago, in its social and historical context.

ARTH 363.course_name: Art in Japan: The Problem with Painting
ARTH 363.description: Key debates in the history of painting and its institutionalization.

ARTH 368.description: Historical and theoretical questions concerning the development of print media in Japan, from Edo period woodcuts to the advent of digital technologies.

ARTH 369.course_name: Art in Japan: Modern Visual Culture
ARTH 369.description: Self and community in the art and visual culture of modern Japan.

ARTH 370.description: Pre-Aztec monumental and portable arts of the Olmec, Zapotec, Teotihuacan and Classic Veracruz peoples.

ARTH 371.course_name: Arts of the Aztec period in Mexico.
ARTH 371.description: Symbolic meanings and political agendas of Aztec architecture, sculpture and manuscript illustration investigated using Spanish accounts.

ARTH 372.description: Architecture, sculpture, costume, and visual productions associated with Maya public ritual, including the ancient ball game and modern cofrada dances.

ARTH 373.description: Social context and meaning of the Maya's elaborate architecture, sculpture, mural paintings, jewelry, ceramics, figurines, and textiles, ancient and modern, of residences from humble to palatial.

ARTH 376.course_name: Arts of the Northwest Coast Peoples: The North
ARTH 376.description: The histories, historiography and cultural diversity of the Northern Northwest Coast region; persistence and innovation in the arts in communities, and in cross-cultural and market spheres.

ARTH 377.course_name: Arts of the Northwest Coast Peoples: The South
ARTH 377.description: The histories, historiography and cultural diversity of the Southern Northwest Coast region; persistence and innovation in the arts in communities, and in cross-cultural and market spheres.

ARTH 380.description: Relationship between artistic practice and media, examined through a history of paradigm shifts in technology.

ARTH 381.description: Critical approach to the figure of the artist in art, film and texts, from the Early Modern period to the present.

ARTH 382.description: Issues in the history of art through the lens of queer theory.

ARTH 383.description: Diverse forms of human contact and creative collaboration, their effects on art and art-making, and their capacity to challenge conventions of artistic genius as dependent on masculinity, singularity, and heteronormativity. ARTH 382 recommended as preparation.

ARTH 386.description: Reparative possibilities of art and art history as ways of sensing and responding to human impact on planetary life.

ARTH 397.description: Thematic and issue-based courses in art history. Topics vary year to year.

ARTH 410.description: Key debates in the art of Africa and the African diaspora. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST_V 410 or ARTH_V 410. Equivalency: AFST_V 410. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
